extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in medical machine learning, systematic reviewers, and clinicians interested in ML model evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: A systematic review of systematic reviews that identifies common types of bias impeding applicability and generalizability of machine learning models in healthcare and appraises methodological quality using standard risk-of-bias tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date range inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Only systematic reviews published between January 1, 2022 and June 1, 2025 were included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and apply a clear date range for eligible studies when performing a review to limit scope and ensure recency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database scope for literature search
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant systematic reviews were identified across three databases: PubMed, Embase and Medline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a standardized, multi-database search strategy (at minimum major biomedical databases) to comprehensively identify eligible reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of included studies (machine learning focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only studies that examined the application of machine learning, including its subfield of deep learning, were included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify whether ML and subfields (e.g., deep learning) are within scope and apply that consistently during screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized tools for risk-of-bias assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Included reviews were required to have employed standardized tools for risk of bias assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require and report use of established risk-of-bias instruments rather than informal or ad-hoc assessments when evaluating primary studies or reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to PRISMA guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional inclusion criteria required that studies adhere to the PRISMA guidelines for systematic reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and report whether reviews follow PRISMA (or equivalent reporting guidance) as a marker of reporting quality and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Included studies had to be published in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare any language restrictions explicitly and consider their potential for introducing selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMSTAR 2 for review-level bias assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk of bias was assessed using a tailored and modified version of the Assessment of Systematic Reviews tool (AMSTAR 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply AMSTAR 2 (tailored as needed) to evaluate methodological limitations of systematic reviews and document any modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROBIS for methodological quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological quality was evaluated according to the Risk of Bias in Systematic Reviews (ROBIS) guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ROBIS to appraise the risk of bias specific to systematic review methods and report findings alongside other quality assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROBAST for primary prediction-model studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk of bias in the primary studies were appraised using PROBAST (n=33).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PROBAST when assessing risk of bias and applicability for prediction-model studies; report counts and contexts in which it was applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: QUADAS-2 for diagnostic accuracy studies
rubrics_metrics.description: QUADAS-2 was used to appraise risk of bias in primary diagnostic accuracy studies (n=17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply QUADAS-2 for diagnostic-model evaluations and report its use and results explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cochrane Handbook approaches for intervention studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Some reviews applied the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Review of Interventions to appraise primary studies (n=3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Cochrane-recommended methods when reviews address intervention-related questions and indicate how these were adapted for ML contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies
rubrics_metrics.description: ROBINS-I was used in some reviews to assess bias in non-randomized studies (n=2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When primary evidence is non-randomized, apply ROBINS-I and describe risk domains considered relevant to ML evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robvis (visualization) reported use
rubrics_metrics.description: Robvis was reported as a tool used in one review (n=1) for visualization of risk-of-bias assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use visualization tools (e.g., Robvis) to transparently present risk-of-bias assessments in reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: QUIPS for prognostic studies
rubrics_metrics.description: QUIPS was used in one review (n=1) to assess bias in prognostic studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use QUIPS for prognostic-problem reviews and report domains assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPHPP for public-health style evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: EPHPP was used in one review (n=1) to appraise study quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider EPHPP where public-health intervention or observational study appraisal is appropriate; state rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined tool applications (e.g., PROBAST & TRIPOD, QUADAS-2 & PROBAST)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some reviews applied combinations of appraisal/reporting tools such as PROBAST & TRIPOD and QUADAS-2 & PROBAST (each n=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining complementary tools for risk-of-bias and reporting guidance can be appropriate; report how tools were integrated and any overlaps or gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of external validation (common source of bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most frequently identified source of bias included lack of external validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether models were externally validated on independent datasets and treat absence of external validation as a major threat to generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical bias (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical bias noted as a frequent source, e.g., inadequate handling of missing data, insufficient sample size, lack of internal validation, and poor reporting of model calibration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess analytic practices comprehensively: handling of missingness, sample size justification, internal validation procedures (e.g., cross-validation, bootstrapping), and transparent reporting of calibration metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant selection bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant selection bias was commonly identified as a source of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine sampling frame, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and representativeness; consider selection mechanisms that could limit applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias related to the reference standard / ground truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias related to the reference standard or ground truth was frequently identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess quality and reliability of labels/ground truth (e.g., diagnostic criteria, chart review, gold-standard tests) and how misclassification may impact model performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature selection bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature selection bias was identified as a common problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether feature selection was performed appropriately (e.g., inside cross-validation) and whether leakage or data-driven selection inflated performance estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model interpretability and algorithmic bias issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues related to model interpretability and algorithmic bias were highlighted among common sources of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess transparency and interpretability of model outputs and check for algorithmic bias (e.g., disparate performance across subgroups); report fairness and explainability analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for standardized methodological guidelines (recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing standardized methodological guidelines for future studies was recommended to improve generalizability and acceptability of ML models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop and follow field-specific standardized methodological and reporting guidelines (e.g., extensions/adaptations of PRISMA, TRIPOD, PROBAST) to enhance reproducibility, generalizability, and safe clinical integration.
